answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making influence earned slowly. Each identity starts with a tiny per-epoch action quota, and reputation grows only through completed jobs that peers verify — a fable of instant influence fails because no shortcut exists. Like vines on a trellis, trust climbs one verified rung at a time, and idle reputation decays, so Sybils cannot be stockpiled in advance. At dawn of each epoch, quotas reset but reputation persists, so an attacker creating a thousand fresh identities still faces weeks of real, verified work before any can sway a vote.
